title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Moon in the Barrel
summary: At the end of every month the nights in Chelm are as black as coal, and everyone bumps into fences and falls into puddles. So the Wise Men of Chelm decide: we'll catch the moon when it's full and save it for the dark nights! They cover it, tie it, seal it and haul it away, but only little Rivkele looks up... A funny rhyming story based on traditional Chelm folk tales.
pages:
In the town of Chelm, when each month comes to an end,
the night is pitch-black, with no moon and no light to lend.
Reb Feivel bumped into a fence: BOOM!
Reb Todros fell into a puddle: PLOOM!

The wise men all met in the synagogue, small and snug,
they scratched at their hats, and their beards got a scratch and a tug.
Then up stood Reb Zainvel, the wisest of all:
"We'll catch the moon when it's full and as round as a ball!"
We are the Wise Men of Chelm, we can solve any problem!

When the moon was full, they brought a barrel, big and stout,
and filled it with water till it almost sloshed out.
They peeked inside, and there, in the water deep within,
was a round yellow moon! "We caught it!" cried the old men with a grin.

"Quick, before it runs off! A sheet, and one sheet more!
A rug, and a rug, and pillows, till the house has no more!"
Rivkele pointed: "But wait... up there, in the sky..."
"Shhh, child! Wise men are busy at night, so don't you pry!"

"Now ropes!" A knot, and a double knot too,
and a red wax seal on top, all the way through!
Rivkele tried again: "But Grandpa, up in the sky..."
"Shhh, child! Wise men are busy at night, so don't you pry!"
We are the Wise Men of Chelm, we can solve any problem!

Ten wise men lifted: OOF! And once more: OOF!
They lugged the barrel to the synagogue, right under its roof.
They set it in a corner, on tiptoe, nice and slow:
"Good night, Moon! See you in a few weeks or so!"

A week went by, then another, and the night turned black.
"It's time!" cried Reb Zainvel. "Let's bring the light back!"
We are the Wise Men of Chelm, we can solve any problem!

They untied knot after knot, pulled off rug and sheet,
they all peeked inside and... nothing! Nothing! Nothing to greet!
Just water, no moon! "Oh dear, what a fright!
Someone stole the moon, and nobody guarded it all night!"

Then little Rivkele pointed to the window and said,
"It's not stolen! Look up there, as thin as a balloon's thread!
It slipped out of the barrel through a tiny hole in the sheet,
and that's why it's so skinny, squashed like a sardine, from its head to its feet!"

And since then, in Chelm, when the month is half through,
they fill up a barrel and seal it anew.
Beside it sits a watchman, awake, with a lantern held tight,
and Rivkele looks up, and the moon winks at her, just at her, in the night.
We are the Wise Men of Chelm, we can solve any problem!
